title: Burstwave Inspector — per-burst metrics, span stitching, and contextual redact orchestration
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Goal: Implement a 'Burstwave Inspector' to provide lightweight per-burst telemetry, deterministic span stitching across burst boundaries and nested tool calls, and an orchestration layer that applies contextual redaction before telemetry sinks.

Background: Current stream telemetry focuses on per-chunk or per-token hooks (many tickets above). We noticed a recurring class of operational questions: noisy short-lived bursts (many tokens emitted in a tight window) skewing latency percentiles, and traces that fragment across client-side reassembly points when tool-calls or structured outputs interleave. Existing redaction is applied either too late (post-aggregation) or too early (losing tracing linkages).

Proposal:
- Define a Burst concept (logical group of emissions within a single request where inter-token gap < 50ms or emitted under the same routing decision). Emit three burst-level telemetry events: burst.start, burst.emit (aggregated at end or periodically), and burst.end. Events should include aggregated metrics (token_count, burst_duration_ms, top_tool_calls, kv_cache_hits, emit_bytes) as well as a burst_id.
- Span stitching: attach a stable burst_id to all spans created during that burst. Implement a stitcher in the tracing pipeline to join child spans across burst.start/end boundaries so UI can show contiguous parent-child relationships for tool-calls and function invocations. Add a 'stitch_hint' attribute to spans output by older SDKs to maintain compatibility.
- Contextual redact orchestration: introduce a redact policy stage that runs immediately after burst.emit but before any telemetry sink that might persist raw content. Policies are configurable per-customer and support (1) grammar-based scrub rules, (2) token-window heuristics (redact last N tokens if sensitive indicator detected), and (3) safe-sampling for debugging (retains 0.1% of raw bursts with customer consent). Redaction must preserve burst_id and trace linkage metadata while replacing sensitive text with deterministic placeholders.
- Compatibility layer: provide a compatibility shim for older SDKs that only emit per-chunk events by mapping chunk boundaries to bursts heuristically and emitting stitch_hint attributes. Document event names and attribute deprecations in a concise compatibility guide so older dashboards keep working.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Aggregating on-burst reduces cardinality but risks masking within-burst skew; we'll expose both aggregated and sampled per-emission metrics for high-value customers.
- Redaction prior to trace sinks increases privacy but complicates debugging; hence opt-in raw-sample path.
- Stitching increases trace payload size slightly (burst_id on many spans) — should be negligible relative to benefit.

Acceptance criteria (see list below) and next steps are included as tasks.
acceptance_criteria: burst.start/emit/end events emitted for >=95% of requests that contain >5 tokens within a 50ms gap threshold
burst-level dashboard with token_count, p50/p95 burst_duration_ms, error_rate and key tool_call counts available in Console
stitcher reconstructs parent->child relationships across burst boundaries for >98% of simulated tool-call sequences in the unit test harness
redact orchestration removes PII patterns (email, SSN, credit_card) per policy in CI tests and retains burst_id/trace metadata
compat shim maps legacy chunk events to bursts with documented heuristics and smoke tests covering SDK v1.8 and v1.9
technical_notes:
Telemetry schema: new event names burst.start, burst.emit, burst.end. burst_id: uuid v4. Attributes: token_count (int), emit_bytes (int), burst_duration_ms (int), predominant_tool (string), kv_cache_hits (int), sampling_reason (string|null).
Trace stitching: add 'burst_id' tag to spans and a 'stitch_hint' boolean for legacy mapping. Stitcher will look for sequence of spans with matching request_id and temporally adjacent timestamps to stitch when burst_id absent.
Redaction: use deterministic placeholders like [REDACTED:EMAIL_HASH] where hash = sha1(lowercase(original_email))[0:8] to help debugging while avoiding exposure.
Compatibility: publish shim package redwood-observability-shim@>=1.2.0 for SDKs.
SLOs impacted: aim to keep 95th token latency delta < 5ms when instrumentation enabled (opt-out flag available per route).
